question.title: Consecutive Logins
question.desc: Find all users who have logged in for at least three consecutive days.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users; CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_name VARCHAR(255)); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS logins; CREATE TABLE logins (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER, login_date DATE); INSERT INTO users (user_name) VALUES ('Alice'), ('Bob'), ('Charlie'); INSERT INTO logins (user_id, login_date) VALUES (1, '2022-01-01'), (1, '2022-01-02'), (1, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-01'), (2, '2022-01-03'), (3, '2022-01-01'), (3, '2022-01-02'), (3, '2022-01-04');
question.solution: WITH consecutive_logins AS ( SELECT user_id, login_date, login_date - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS consecutive_group FROM logins ), consecutive_sequences AS ( SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS consecutive_days FROM consecutive_logins GROUP BY user_id, consecutive_group ) SELECT u.user_name, cs.consecutive_days FROM users u JOIN consecutive_sequences cs ON u.id = cs.user_id WHERE cs.consecutive_days >= 3;
question.tips: Consider using window functions to track consecutive sequences.
hints: You may need to use a subquery or CTE to first identify consecutive login dates for each user.
Use ROW_NUMBER() to assign a unique number to each login date for each user, and then subtract this from the login date to identify consecutive groups.
Join the users table with the result of the consecutive sequences query to get the user names.
